ordered_diagnoses: Bicuspid Aortic Valve with Aortic Aneurysm

facts.raw_span: A 58-year-old male
with an unremarkable medical history
presented with a 2-year history of chest tightness on exertion and shortness of breath
He had two episodes of acute onset syncope with an unknown cause
No specific physical examination findings were reported in the case
Revealed ascending aortic aneurysm with diameters of ascending aorta and sinus of Valsalva at 49mm and 40mm respectively
Revealed mild aortic regurgitation of the bicuspid aortic valve
Demonstrated slow blood perfusion in the left coronary artery, without evidence of significant atherosclerosis
No abnormalities
Organized thrombus measuring 1 × 0.8 cm found at the left coronary cusp of the aortic valve, covering most of the left coronary artery's ostium
Confirmed the excised mass as an organized thrombus
Transcranial Doppler (TCD): No abnormalities
